query: How will the restriction on investments for the first $20,000 in Ordinary Account and the first $40,000 in Special Account affect me?
reference_answer: The first $60,000 of your combined CPF accounts earns an extra 1% interest. To enable members to earn extra interest, only monies in excess of $20,000 in your Ordinary Account (OA) and $40,000 in your Special Account (SA) can be invested.However, you can continue to service your agent bank fees and regular premium insurance policies (excludes recurring single premium insurance policies or regular savings plans for unit trusts) even if your OA balance falls below $20,000.If you have already made investments using your OA or SA balances, you are not required to sell these investments.

The co-insurance for the first $5,000 claimable amount is $300, calculated as 10% of the remaining $3,000 beyond the $2,000 deductible.

You can continue to service the future premiums using your Ordinary Account savings, even if your balance falls below $20,000. This applies to you even after age 55 as long as you have set aside the Full Retirement Sum or the Basic Retirement Sum with sufficient property charge/pledge in the Retirement Account.

It takes into account not only the realised profits or losses of investments that were sold, but also the unrealised profits or losses of investments that members held during the reporting period.
answer: The restriction means only excess funds over $20,000 in Ordinary Account and $40,000 in Special Account can be invested. This affects earning extra interest. However, you can still manage regular expenses and insurance payments, even if balances fall below these limits. [Document 1]
